a [[card game]]. #: {{ux|en|He played '''cards''' with his friends.}} # A [[resource]] or [[argument]], used to achieve a purpose. {{q|See {{m|en|play the something card}}.}} #: {{ux|en|The government played the Orange '''card''' to get support for their Ireland policy.}} #: {{ux|en|He accused them of [[play the race card|playing the race '''card''']].}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2007|author=Luke McNamara|title=Human Rights Controversies: The Impact of Legal Form|page=138|passage=Having adopted civil union as their goal, proponents of the Civil Union Bill were sensitive to the need not to overplay the human rights '''card''', aware that there was a significant degree of resistance in the New Zealand {{...}}}} # A [[bank card]]. # Any electronic payment (rather than a cash payment using notes, bills or coins). #: {{ux|en|Cashier: "Cash or '''card'''? Customer: "I'm paying on my phone, so '''card'''."}} # {{lb|en|uncountable}} [[paper|Paper]] that is thicker and more durable than normal writing or printing paper, but thinner and more flexible than [[paperboard]], used for postcards, playing cards, etc.; [[card stock]]. #: {{ux|en|Do you have any '''card'''? I want to make a poster.}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} A [[map]] or [[chart]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1590|author=w:Edmund Spenser|title=w:The Faerie Queene|section=II.vii|passage=As pilot well expert in perilous waue, / Vpon his '''card''' and compas firmes his eye {{...}}.}} # {{lb|en|informal}} An [[amusing]] or [[entertaining]] person, often [[slightly]] [[eccentric]]. #* {{quote-web|en|year=2007|author=w:Meredith Gran|url=http://www.octopuspie.com/2007-11-12/071-deadpan/|title=Octopus Pie #71: Deadpan |site=octopuspie.com |passage=MAREK: But really the deadpan is key. EVE: Oh, Marek, you '''card'''.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1963|author=w:Sylvia Plath|title=s:The Bell Jar|publisher=Faber and Faber |passage='What a '''card'''!' Doreen said. 'Isn't he a '''card'''?'}} # A list of scheduled events or of performers or contestants; chiefly used in [[professional wrestling]]. #: {{ux|en|What's on the '''card''' for tonight?}} # {{lb|en|cricket}} A [[tabular]] [[presentation]] of the [[key]] [[statistics]] of an [[innings]] or [[match]]: [[batsman|batsmen]]’s [[score]]s and how they were [[dismissed]], [[extras]], total score and [[bowling figures]]. # {{lb|en|computing}} A removable electronic device that may be inserted into a powered electronic device to provide additional capability. #: {{syn|en|expansion card}} #: {{ux|en|He needed to replace the '''card''' his computer used to connect to the internet.}} # {{lb|en|computing}} Any of a set of [[page]]s or [[form]]s that the user can [[navigate]] between, and fill with [[data]], in certain [[user interface]]s. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1993|author=Danny Goodman|title=The Complete HyperCard 2.2 Handbook|page=198 |passage=The button will "see" the cursor through a '''card''' domain graphic; you can then change button graphics on each '''card'''.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2008|author=Johan Hjelm|title=Why IPTV?: Interactivity, Technologies, Services|page=13 |passage=The interaction model of WAP, originally developed for mobile phones to interact with information services in a web-like way, was based on Apple's HyperCard, and instead of pages, the user interacted with a deck of '''cards''', which were interlinked by a scripting language.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2012|author=Veljko Milutinovic; Frédéric Patricelli|title=Mastering E-Business Infrastructure|page=329 |passage=The basic building blocks of WML applications are '''cards'''. '''Cards''' are equivalent to HTML pages. Just as Web browser can show only one page at a time (except when using frames), a WAP enabled device can also show only one '''card''' at a time.}} # A [[greeting card]]. #: {{ux|en|She gave her neighbors a '''card''' congratulating them on their new baby.}} # A [[business card]]. #: {{ux|en|The realtor gave me her '''card''' so I could call if I had any questions about buying a house.}} # {{lb|en|television}} A [[title card]] or [[intertitle]]: a piece of filmed, printed text edited into the midst of the photographed action at various points, generally to convey character dialogue or descriptive narrative material related to the plot. # A [[test card]]. # In [[formal]] [[debate|debating]], a [[verbatim]] [[citation]] used as [[evidence]] for a [[point]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=2011|author=N. Andre Cossette|title=The Art of Debate: 12th Edition|page=123 |passage=You can make most theory answers without '''cards''', but some '''cards''' do exist which specifically criticize [[kritik]]s on a theoretical basis.}} # {{lb|en|dated}} A published note, containing a brief statement, explanation, request, expression of thanks, etc. #: {{co|en|to put a '''card''' in the newspapers}} # {{lb|en|dated}} A printed [[programme]]. # {{lb|en|dated|figurative|by extension}} An [[attraction]] or [[inducement]]. #: {{ux|en|This will be a good '''card''' for the last day of the fair.}} # {{lb|en|nautical}} {{ellipsis of|en|compass card}}. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1594|author=Richard Hooker|title=Laws of Ecclesiastical Polity|section=1.2.5|page=153 (Everyman edition, vol. 1)|passage="The Lord possessed me [= Wisdom] in the beginning of his way, even before his works of old was I set up;" that law, which hath been the pattern to make, and is the '''card''' to guide the world by}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Macbeth|I|iii|passage=All the quarters that they know / I' the shipman's '''card'''.}} # {{lb|en|weaving}} A perforated [[pasteboard]] or sheet-metal plate for [[warp]] [[thread]]s, making part of the Jacquard apparatus of a [[loom]]. # {{lb|en|graph theory}} A [[graph]] formed from a given graph by deleting one [[vertex]]. #: {{cot|en|deck}} # An [[indicator card]]. # {{lb|en|Philippines|education}} {{ellipsis of|en|report card}}. #: {{ux|en|Where's your '''card'''? It is used principally with raw cotton, wool, hair, or other natural fibers to prepare these materials for spinning into [[yarn]] or [[thread]] on a [[spinning wheel]], with a [[whorl]] or other hand-held [[spindle]].
